addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Behavioral verifier for flutter__flutter-181500-mm.
3	# Applies the PR test additions, runs f2p+p2p tests, computes reward.
4	# NEVER greps source for the fix — scores from test execution only.
5	set -uo pipefail
6	mkdir -p /logs/verifier
7	STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
8	STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
9	REPORT=/logs/verifier/report.json
10	
11	: > "$STDOUT_LOG"; : > "$STDERR_LOG"
12	
13	ensure_reward() { [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; }
14	trap ensure_reward EXIT
15	
16	cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }
17	
18	# Explicit PATH for flutter tool (also set by Dockerfile ENV)
19	export PATH="/opt/flutter/bin:${PATH}"
20	
21	# Restore any test files the agent may have edited to their pristine base state
22	# BEFORE applying test.patch, so agent edits to tests cannot influence scoring.
23	echo "== restoring test files from harbor_base ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
24	for _p in $(grep '^+++ b/' /tests/test.patch | sed 's#^+++ b/##'); do
25	  git checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null \
26	    || rm -f "/app/$_p" 2>/dev/null || true
27	done
28	
29	echo "== applying test.patch ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
30	git apply --binary /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
31	  || git apply /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
32	  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
33	  || { echo "ERROR: could not apply test.patch" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }
34	
35	echo "== building name regex from config.json ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
36	PATTERN=$(python3 - <<'PYEOF'
37	import re, json
38	c = json.load(open('/tests/config.json'))
39	names = c.get('f2p', []) + c.get('p2p', [])
40	print('|'.join('(?:' + re.escape(n) + ')' for n in names))
41	PYEOF
42	) || { echo "ERROR: failed to build test name pattern" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }
43	
44	echo "pattern: $PATTERN" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
45	
46	# flutter test must run from within packages/flutter/ (not the monorepo root)
47	echo "== running f2p + p2p tests ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
48	cd /app/packages/flutter
49	flutter test \
50	  test/material/date_range_picker_test.dart \
51	  --name "$PATTERN" \
52	  --reporter json > "$REPORT" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
53	  || echo "(flutter test exited non-zero; parsing report)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
54	
55	echo "== computing reward ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
56	# Rubric judge - SUB-AGENT backend: no API key, no network. On the first pass there is no
57	# verdict yet, so judge.py writes a judge request under /logs/verifier/judge/ and prints

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Behavioral verifier for flutter__flutter-181500-mm.
# Applies the PR test additions, runs f2p+p2p tests, computes reward.
# NEVER greps source for the fix — scores from test execution only.
set -uo pipefail
mkdir -p /logs/verifier
STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
REPORT=/logs/verifier/report.json

: > "$STDOUT_LOG"; : > "$STDERR_LOG"

ensure_reward() { [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; }
trap ensure_reward EXIT

cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# Explicit PATH for flutter tool (also set by Dockerfile ENV)
export PATH="/opt/flutter/bin:${PATH}"

# Restore any test files the agent may have edited to their pristine base state
# BEFORE applying test.patch, so agent edits to tests cannot influence scoring.
echo "== restoring test files from harbor_base ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
for _p in $(grep '^+++ b/' /tests/test.patch | sed 's#^+++ b/##'); do
  git checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null \
    || rm -f "/app/$_p" 2>/dev/null || true
done

echo "== applying test.patch ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
git apply --binary /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || git apply /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: could not apply test.patch" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

echo "== building name regex from config.json ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
PATTERN=$(python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import re, json
c = json.load(open('/tests/config.json'))
names = c.get('f2p', []) + c.get('p2p', [])
print('|'.join('(?:' + re.escape(n) + ')' for n in names))
PYEOF
) || { echo "ERROR: failed to build test name pattern" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

echo "pattern: $PATTERN" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

# flutter test must run from within packages/flutter/ (not the monorepo root)
echo "== running f2p + p2p tests ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
cd /app/packages/flutter
flutter test \
  test/material/date_range_picker_test.dart \
  --name "$PATTERN" \
  --reporter json > "$REPORT" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || echo "(flutter test exited non-zero; parsing report)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

echo "== computing reward ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
# Rubric judge - SUB-AGENT backend: no API key, no network. On the first pass there is no
# verdict yet, so judge.py writes a judge request under /logs/verifier/judge/ and prints
# nothing. The `|| echo ""` is load-bearing: the judge must never be able to fail the run.
RUBRIC=""
if [ -f /tests/rubrics.json ]; then
  RUBRIC=$(python3 /tests/judge.py --rubrics /tests/rubrics.json --repo /app \
             2>/logs/verifier/judge.log || echo "")
  echo "Rubric verdict: ${RUBRIC:-pending (judge request written; rescore after grading)}"
fi

python3 /tests/verifier.py 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
echo "reward=$(cat /logs/verifier/reward.txt 2>/dev/null)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Reward policy (all flutter multimodal tasks):
3	  1.0  — every f2p passes AND every p2p passes
4	  0.5  — some f2p pass but not all, OR any p2p regressed
5	  0.0  — no f2p passes or report absent / suite failed to compile
6	
7	Behavioral only: reads `flutter test --reporter json` output; NEVER inspects source.
8	"""
9	import json
10	import os
11	import re
12	
13	CONF   = json.load(open('/tests/config.json'))
14	F2P    = CONF['f2p']
15	P2P    = CONF['p2p']
16	REPORT = '/logs/verifier/report.json'
17	REWARD = '/logs/verifier/reward.txt'
18	
19	
20	def load_results():
21	    """Parse `flutter test --reporter json` events → {test_name: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'}."""
22	    if not os.path.exists(REPORT):
23	        return {}
24	    results = {}
25	    id_to_name = {}
26	    for raw in open(REPORT, errors='replace'):
27	        raw = raw.strip()
28	        if not raw:
29	            continue
30	        try:
31	            ev = json.loads(raw)
32	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
33	            continue
34	        etype = ev.get('type', '')
35	        if etype == 'testStart':
36	            t = ev.get('test', {})
37	            id_to_name[t.get('id')] = t.get('name', '')
38	        elif etype == 'testDone':
39	            tid  = ev.get('testID')
40	            name = id_to_name.get(tid, str(tid))
41	            res  = ev.get('result', 'error')   # 'success' | 'failure' | 'error'
42	            skip = ev.get('skipped', False)
43	            if skip:
44	                results[name] = 'skip'
45	            elif res == 'success':
46	                results[name] = 'pass'
47	            else:
48	                results[name] = 'fail'
49	    return results
50	
51	
52	def match_ident(ident, results):
53	    """Substring-tolerant match: first hit wins."""
54	    for name, val in results.items():
55	        if ident == name or ident in name or re.search(re.escape(ident), name):
56	            return val
57	    return 'missing'
58	
59	
60	def main():
61	    r    = load_results()
62	    f2p  = {k: match_ident(k, r) for k in F2P}
63	    p2p  = {k: match_ident(k, r) for k in P2P}
64	
65	    f2p_pass = [k for k, v in f2p.items() if v == 'pass']
66	    p2p_pass = [k for k, v in p2p.items() if v == 'pass']
67	
68	    all_f2p  = len(f2p_pass) == len(F2P) and len(F2P) > 0
69	    all_p2p  = len(p2p_pass) == len(P2P)
70	
71	    if all_f2p and all_p2p:
72	        reward = 1.0
73	    elif f2p_pass:          # partial f2p pass, or p2p regression
74	        reward = 0.5
75	    else:
76	        reward = 0.0        # no f2p passed (includes compile error / empty report)
77	
78	    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(REWARD), exist_ok=True)
79	    with open(REWARD, 'w') as fh:
80	        fh.write(str(reward))
81	    print(json.dumps({'reward': reward, 'f2p': f2p, 'p2p': p2p}))
82	
83	
84	if __name__ == '__main__':
85	    main()
86

51	    r"(\.test\.[jt]sx?$|\.spec\.[jt]sx?$|(^|/)tests?/|(^|/)__tests__/|"

161	        if v < 1.0:                            # strictly binary: only a full 1 passes
162	            failed.append(c["id"])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Rubric judge — sub-agent backend. NO API KEY, NO NETWORK.

Binary and unweighted: every criterion is PASS/FAIL and every one is mandatory, so the
rubric passes only if all pass.

Two-phase, mirroring ProjectBench's tier3 sub-agent backend:

  Phase 1 (during the verifier run)
      No verdict exists yet, so this writes a self-contained judge request into the judge
      dir -- criteria_payload.json, source.txt (the candidate diff), PROMPT.md -- prints
      nothing, and exits 0. The verifier then scores on tests alone.

  Phase 2 (after the run, orchestrated outside the container)
      A judge sub-agent reads PROMPT.md and writes verdict.json next to it. Re-running this
      script (or `mm_run.sh <task> rescore`) reads that verdict and prints "pass" or "fail".

Because the judge never calls out, there is no proxy, no bridge, no credentials, and no
[verifier.env] block anywhere.

Contract (test.sh depends on all three):
  * prints "pass" or "fail" on stdout, or NOTHING when no verdict is available yet
  * writes the per-criterion detail to <judge dir>/summary.json
  * ALWAYS exits 0, so the judge can never fail the run

Env:
  PB_JUDGE_DIR      where the request/verdict live (default /logs/verifier/judge)
  PB_JUDGE_VERDICT  explicit path to verdict.json (overrides the default location)

IMPORTANT: never name a file in tests/ after a stdlib module (select.py, json.py, types.py,
io.py, queue.py). It shadows the real module and the failure surfaces somewhere unrelated.
The sys.path strip below defends against it.
"""
import os
import sys

_self_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path[:] = [p for p in sys.path if os.path.abspath(p or os.getcwd()) != _self_dir]

import argparse
import json
import re
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

DEFAULT_JUDGE_DIR = "/logs/verifier/judge"
# Hunks for these paths never reach the judge: it must grade the fix, not the harness the
# submission may have edited.
EXCLUDE_RE = re.compile(
    r"(\.test\.[jt]sx?$|\.spec\.[jt]sx?$|(^|/)tests?/|(^|/)__tests__/|"
    r"(^|/)__snapshots__/|(^|/)node_modules/|(^|/)\.git/)"
)
BASE_REFS = ("harbor_base", "HEAD")

JUDGE_SYSTEM = (
    "You are a strict senior engineer grading the APPROACH of a code change -- not whether "
    "its tests pass. Score each rubric criterion STRICTLY BINARY: 1 = fully satisfied, "
    "0 = not satisfied. There is NO partial credit: if a criterion is only partially met, "
    "ambiguous, or has no clear evidence, score 0. Be strict; when unsure, score 0."
)


def judge_dir() -> Path:
    return Path(os.environ.get("PB_JUDGE_DIR") or DEFAULT_JUDGE_DIR)


def candidate_diff(repo: str, budget: int = 120_000) -> str:
    for ref in BASE_REFS:
        try:
            out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "diff", ref],
                                 capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
        except Exception as exc:
            sys.stderr.write("[judge] git diff failed: %s\n" % exc)
            return ""
        if out.returncode == 0 and out.stdout.strip():
            sys.stderr.write("[judge] diffing against %s\n" % ref)
            return filter_diff(out.stdout, budget)
    sys.stderr.write("[judge] no non-empty diff found\n")
    return ""


def filter_diff(diff: str, budget: int) -> str:
    kept, cur, keep = [], [], True
    for line in diff.splitlines(keepends=True):
        if line.startswith("diff --git "):
            if keep and cur:
                kept.extend(cur)
            parts = line.split()
            path = parts[-1][2:] if len(parts) >= 4 else ""
            keep = not EXCLUDE_RE.search(path)
            cur = [line]
        else:
            cur.append(line)
    if keep and cur:
        kept.extend(cur)
    blob = "".join(kept)
    return blob[:budget] + "\n[... truncated ...]\n" if len(blob) > budget else blob


def write_request(criteria, diff, jdir: Path) -> None:
    """Lay down everything a judge sub-agent needs, with no further context."""
    jdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    payload = [{"id": c["id"], "criterion": c["criterion"]} for c in criteria]
    (jdir / "criteria_payload.json").write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))
    (jdir / "source.txt").write_text(diff)
    verdict = jdir / "verdict.json"
    ids = ", ".join(c["id"] for c in criteria)
    (jdir / "PROMPT.md").write_text(f"""# Rubric judge (sub-agent)

You are the rubric judge. Grade the APPROACH of a code change, not whether its tests pass.

System contract:
{JUDGE_SYSTEM}

Inputs in this directory ({jdir}):
- `criteria_payload.json` — {len(criteria)} criteria, each {{id, criterion}}.
- `source.txt` — the candidate diff. Test, spec and snapshot files are already stripped out,
  so everything you see is product code the submission changed.

Score each criterion **1 or 0 — never 0.5 or any fraction**. 1 = fully satisfied,
0 = not satisfied, ambiguous, or no clear evidence. Be strict; when unsure, score 0.

The rubric is unweighted and every criterion is mandatory: a single 0 fails the whole rubric,
so do not withhold a 1 over style preferences the criterion does not actually state.

Write ONLY this JSON to `{verdict}`:

    {{"scores": {{"<criterion id>": {{"score": 0|1}}, ...}}}}

All {len(criteria)} ids must appear: {ids}. Verify the file parses before you finish.
""")


def read_verdict(criteria, jdir: Path):
    """Return ("pass"|"fail", failed_ids) or None when no usable verdict exists."""
    vp = Path(os.environ.get("PB_JUDGE_VERDICT") or (jdir / "verdict.json"))
    if not vp.is_file():
        return None
    try:
        obj = json.loads(vp.read_text())
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict unreadable (%s)\n" % exc)
        return None
    scores = obj.get("scores", obj)
    if not isinstance(scores, dict):
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict has no scores map\n")
        return None
    failed, graded = [], 0
    for c in criteria:
        raw = scores.get(c["id"])
        if raw is None:
            failed.append(c["id"])            # not graded == not demonstrated == fail
            continue
        try:
            v = float(raw.get("score") if isinstance(raw, dict) else raw)
        except (TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError):
            failed.append(c["id"])
            continue
        graded += 1
        if v < 1.0:                            # strictly binary: only a full 1 passes
            failed.append(c["id"])
    if graded == 0:
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict contained no usable scores\n")
        return None
    return ("fail" if failed else "pass"), failed


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--rubrics", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--repo", default="/app")
    ap.add_argument("--judge-dir", default=None)
    a = ap.parse_args()

    jdir = Path(a.judge_dir) if a.judge_dir else judge_dir()
    try:
        doc = json.load(open(a.rubrics))
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] cannot read %s: %s\n" % (a.rubrics, exc))
        return 0
    criteria = [c for c in (doc.get("criteria") or []) if c.get("id") and c.get("criterion")]
    if not criteria:
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] no criteria in %s\n" % a.rubrics)
        return 0

    # Phase 2: a verdict is already there -> score it.
    res = read_verdict(criteria, jdir)
    if res is not None:
        verdict, failed = res
        try:
            jdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            json.dump({"rubric": verdict, "failed": failed,
                       "criteria_total": len(criteria)},
                      open(jdir / "summary.json", "w"), indent=2)
        except Exception:
            pass
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] verdict=%s%s\n"
                         % (verdict, (" failed=%s" % ", ".join(failed)) if failed else ""))
        print(verdict)
        return 0

    # Phase 1: no verdict yet -> lay down the request and stay silent.
    diff = candidate_diff(a.repo)
    if not diff.strip():
        sys.stderr.write("[judge] empty candidate diff; nothing to grade\n")
        return 0
    write_request(criteria, diff, jdir)
    sys.stderr.write(
        "[judge] no verdict at %s yet; wrote the judge request to %s "
        "(criteria_payload.json, source.txt, PROMPT.md). Have the judge sub-agent produce "
        "verdict.json, then rescore. Scoring on tests alone until then.\n"
        % (jdir / "verdict.json", jdir))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

FROM ubuntu:22.04

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV FLUTTER_HOME=/opt/flutter
ENV PATH="${FLUTTER_HOME}/bin:${FLUTTER_HOME}/bin/cache/dart-sdk/bin:${PATH}"

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    curl git unzip xz-utils zip libglu1-mesa wget ca-certificates \
    clang cmake ninja-build pkg-config libgtk-3-dev liblzma-dev \
    python3 python3-pip \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /app

# Clone flutter/flutter, pin to base commit, strip .git for anti-cheat,
# then re-init with a single base commit + immutable tag.
RUN git clone https://github.com/flutter/flutter /opt/flutter \
 && git -C /opt/flutter checkout 96d292fa0acd9d11e85fd04f7355a47cf3fb2723 \
 && /opt/flutter/bin/flutter --version

RUN git clone https://github.com/flutter/flutter /app \
 && git -C /app checkout 96d292fa0acd9d11e85fd04f7355a47cf3fb2723 \
 && rm -rf /app/.git \
 && git -C /app init -q \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h add -A \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h commit -q -m base \
 && git -C /app tag harbor_base

# Pre-install Flutter dependencies
RUN cd /app && /opt/flutter/bin/flutter pub get --directory packages/flutter 2>/dev/null || true

# Visual evidence, readable by agent at /app/.harbor_assets/
RUN mkdir -p /logs /app/.harbor_assets
COPY assets/ /app/.harbor_assets/

CMD ["bash"]
